patterns.pattern: إِذَا + [Past-tense verb clause] + سَـ[Present-tense verb clause]
patterns.exampleEnglish: If I go to the airport, I will travel.
patterns.grammarNote: إِذَا ('if') introduces a conditional clause. Formal MSA pairs إِذَا with a PAST-tense verb even when the meaning is future or hypothetical — ذَهَبْتُ here doesn't mean 'I went', it means 'if I go / were I to go', reusing the exact past-tense forms from level 22 rather than minting new ones — the same trick لَمْ/لَنْ/سَـ used to reuse the present-tense pool in levels 32 and 41. The result clause (what happens 'then') is just a normal سَـ-future sentence from level 41. No separate word for 'then' is needed — the two clauses simply follow each other, the same way وَ-joined capstone sentences do.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the tiles to say 'If I go to the airport, I will travel.'
